results.note: Drops the guard that skips repo_root itself, so _worktree_of can return repo_root as the default branch's worktree and the GitHub step would run git in the private checkout.
Exact branch match becomes a substring match, so 'main' also matches 'main-old' (or 'dev' matches 'develop') and the wrong worktree is picked.
Without --verify, show-ref matches by pattern tail, which brings back the old loose match the docstring says was fixed.
Removes the early return when there is no worktree. The step then falls through to the assumed github_root, which is the 'do nothing when there is none' contract broken.
Hardcodes 'main' and ignores the configured default_branch, so a repo whose default is 'master' or 'trunk' finds no worktree, or the wrong one.
Flips the default, so GitHub integration is off unless it is explicitly enabled.
Raises before the private branch is checked out again, so a failed create leaves the repo on a public branch.
A verification failure is only logged and no longer fails the create, which brings back the old warning-only behaviour.
A build exception is swallowed with only a log line, and the create exits 0.

results.note: Drops --cached on the 'file still exists' path, so git rm deletes the person's file from the working folder (the private checkout).
Dry run still really removes files from the index.
Drops the basename step, so patterns like '.env' or '*.log' no longer match nested tracked files such as 'sub/.env', and those stay in the public index.
